Researcher field checklist

2nd Chance Housing, Inc. Researcher training · Draft for organizational and counsel review · Statutes and official pages last read 10/29/2026 · Not legal advice.

Rule for every line: done means the evidence is obtained and checked, not that a field is filled. Unknown stays blank. Stop and ask when you reach a line marked ESCALATE.

1. The lead log (one line per lead)

Lead #Date / initialsChannelWhat I saw or read (their words)Saved as (file name)Status

Channels: walk (public sidewalk only), obituary, records (recorder, assessor, treasurer), court (existing proceedings). A lead is not proof. Name files like L-0003_recorder-search_PIN-001_2026-04-05.pdf.

2. Before you approach the family

  • Searched the Clerk's Recordings for every PIN and saved each result with the search date and the index-through date.
  • Checked for an existing estate case and for a lawyer already acting. ESCALATE if either exists.
  • Have the organization's card and the approved consent form from my supervisor.
  • I will say the four things: who we are; what we offer; what we cannot promise; how to say no.

3. First contact and consent

  • Said the four things. Did not imply any court, county, city or agency sent me.
  • Confirmed who I am speaking with and how they are related. Did not accept a stranger's claim.
  • Signed consent obtained: collect, store, share (with whom), contact preferences, how to withdraw.
  • Wrote down: date, time, who, what they agreed to, and how they want to be contacted.

4. Intake (one or more sittings)

  • The person who died: legal name, other names, date and place of death, county of residence, marital status.
  • The property: address, every PIN, occupancy, tenants, rent, insurance, taxes, mortgage.
  • Papers: death certificate, deed, will or trust, any TODI; who holds each original.
  • Family: every spouse or partner, every child (adopted, earlier relationships, deceased), every earlier death; whereabouts.
  • Their goal (keep, share, sell, refinance), in their words.

5. Urgent-issues screen (ask every time)

  • Tax-sale or tax-delinquency notice?
  • Foreclosure or lender letter?
  • Insurance cancellation, non-renewal, vacancy?
  • Dangerous conditions (heat, fire, structure)?
  • Lawsuit, court date or lawyer letter?

If yes to any: photograph both sides and the envelope (with permission); copy every date exactly into Urgent deadlines; a second person checks the date; ESCALATE the same day by phone and email to my supervisor. Do not tell the family what it means or what to do.

6. Evidence and system entries

  • Before every upload: title, decedent name and one PIN on screen match the paper in my hand.
  • Entered facts exactly as written. Left unknowns blank. Wrote each fact's source in the note.
  • After a save: watched the bar say All changes saved, then reloaded and checked the value is still there.
  • Death certificate fields typed by a person and compared to the scan by a second person. (The page does not read the certificate.)
  • Heirs: every spouse, child and earlier death entered or written as an unresolved question. Not ticked complete until double-checked.
  • Plan facts ticked only where I hold the evidence.

7. Unresolved questions (keep every one)

#QuestionWhy it mattersWho can answerHow I will find outStatus

8. Quality control and handoff

  • Second person compared identity, dates, every PIN, legal description, family and shares, route, amounts, signatures, notary, privacy, version.
  • Numbered file set, evidence index, originals register and unresolved-issues sheet complete.
  • One-page cover memo says what is unresolved first.
  • Sent to counsel on: ____ . Counsel's reply saved. Accepted / Needs changes / Declined: ____ . Counsel's written approval is on file (a typed name or checkbox in the system is not approval).

9. Never

  • Claim to be a court, county, city or government worker, or a law firm.
  • Promise free counsel, ownership, eligibility, savings or results.
  • Pressure, return after a no, enter private grounds, or touch mail.
  • Use a deceased person's login, card or PIN; treat an old power of attorney as the estate's authority.
  • Send a waiver of notice before the petition is filed; sign anything for anyone; backdate.
  • Give legal advice: choose a route, say who inherits, or explain what a notice means.
